solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A power described by simple physicist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be described by something is to have a line drawn round you, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than
P is the standard symbol for power

explanation.surface: A physics lecturer describing power in simple terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The power symbol sits inside the word for simple, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist after whom the unit of electric current is named.

clue.text: Hair growth over parting is bound to be longer

indicators.note: something parting is split in two, with another piece placed in the gap

parts.note: must expresses obligation, being bound to
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A moustache over a hair parting will inevitably grow longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting' looks like part of a hairstyle, but it tells you the word for 'is bound to' splits to take the cricket over; 'longer' is one who longs, not 'more long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is a growth of hair on the upper lip.

clue.text: Funny English farm animals

definitions.note: used as a noun: a funny is a joke

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
first farm animal
second farm animal, the plural covering both

explanation.surface: Remarking that English livestock are amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' reads as an adjective, but it is a noun here, a quip.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying, so it is a funny in the sense of a joke or quip.

clue.text: Highly courteous when one goes for a project

indicators.note: one leaving and a coming in for it means a letter swap, I out and A in

parts.note: extra as an intensifier, as in extra special
polite means courteous
I is the Roman numeral one, the letter removed
taken as written, the letter put in

explanation.surface: Someone being especially courteous when an individual goes for a project.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA POLITE becomes EXTRAPOLATE once the I is swapped for an A.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project known trends forward to estimate unknown values.

clue.text: Partnership for one out of loyalty

indicators.note: out of here means taken away from, so letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: allegiance is loyalty
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A partnership built on loyalty, one example being cited.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the abbreviation for 'for example' from ALLEGIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a partnership or union formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches?

definitions.text: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches?

parts.words: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches
parts.note: surface reading: a bestselling title stocked in every branch of a bookshop chain
setter's reading: branches are also arms of a tree, and the book is a Hemingway novel whose title also suggests leaving arms behind

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun on branches as limbs; the book is Hemingway's 1929 war novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous novel a chain bookshop would stock, and its title punningly bids goodbye to limbs, which branches are.

clue.text: See power cut off

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: An instruction to witness a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cut' reads as a blackout, but the definition is 'cut off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lop is to cut off a branch or limb.

clue.text: It supplies our occupying forces

indicators.note: a force occupying territory sits within it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: the army is the armed forces
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that provides for our troops abroad in occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It supplies' is a cryptic description: the definition sketches what the place does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a store of weapons from which troops are supplied with arms.

clue.text: Split open part of head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the past tense of cleave, to split apart
second meaning: one segment of a head of garlic

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a head wound, but the head is a bulb of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the old past tense of cleave, to divide, and one segment of a garlic bulb.

clue.text: All showers are relaxing here

parts.note: surface reading: a spa or campsite where everyone unwinds under the showers
setter's reading: showers are people who show themselves, exhibiting everything

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'showers' as those who show, not washing facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: At a naturist resort everyone goes unclothed, so every guest is showing all while relaxing.

clue.text: Drop anchor in low river

parts.note: to low is what cattle do
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Anchoring a boat in a shallow river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for shallow water, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to secure it, as by dropping anchor or tying up.

clue.text: Those involved in a domestic row

definitions.text: Those involved in a domestic row

parts.words: Those involved in a domestic row
parts.note: surface reading: people caught up in a family quarrel
setter's reading: a row of homes, dwellings joined in a line

explanation.walkthrough: A row rhyming with 'cow' becomes a row rhyming with 'go'; these are homes built in a joined line, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Such homes share side walls and stand in a continuous line, so each is part of a row of dwellings.

clue.text: In which large sums of money are wasted?

definitions.text: In which large sums of money are wasted?

parts.words: In which large sums of money are wasted?
parts.note: surface reading: a field where big amounts of cash get squandered
setter's reading: wasted is slang for intoxicated, so the money is stoned

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' means squandered on the surface but is slang for drugged, as is 'high'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the world of big-money banking and investment, where the money involved is very large.

clue.text: School maiden has to discharge gas

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to ooze is to discharge slowly

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl forced to release gas, a crude picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is a verb meaning chat, not a vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: To schmooze is to chat in a friendly, ingratiating way, which is what gassing means informally.

clue.text: Country chap's anecdotes

parts.note: a guy is a chap
ana is a collection of anecdotes about a person

explanation.surface: A man's stories about his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of sayings or anecdotes, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a nation on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Places for young railway workers on train

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
a train of events is a series

explanation.surface: Junior rail staff working aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a sequence, not a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurseries are rooms or establishments where young children, or young plants, are cared for.

clue.text: A short tug, and snake gets rodent

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden tug
a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake catches a small mammal after a quick pull.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final K from JERK, then add BOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerboa is a desert-dwelling jumping rodent of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: See red hair

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a short stiff hair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to look at red hair, but 'see red' is the idiom for get angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for reacting with angry indignation and a noun for a stiff animal hair.

clue.text: Playing fragile old French organ

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters get moved about

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Performing on a delicate antique French church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' means a newspaper, the mouthpiece of a party or group, not a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Figaro is a leading daily newspaper in France, and an organ is a publication.

clue.text: Old lady wants it — a cold dish

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an old lady
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grandma demanding a chilled dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'a cold dish' look like a separate phrase, but its 'a' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is an Italian semi-frozen dessert of flavoured crushed ice.

clue.text: Is it overly sweet?

parts.note: surface reading: a question about something too sugary
setter's reading: overly as turned over, so a sweet dessert baked and then flipped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overly' seems to mean excessively but here means inverted.
explanation.definitionFit: This pudding is baked with fruit at the bottom and then inverted to serve, so it is a sweet that has been turned over.

clue.text: Is mother initially proud of us?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: the opening letter of proud
ours means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Wondering whether mum is pleased with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'be mother' is a British idiom for pouring the tea for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever pours the tea at a gathering is said to be mother, so one who pours 'is mother'.

clue.text: Almost completely stop

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: quite can mean completely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: Nearly giving up something entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost completely' reads as one phrase, but 'almost' trims QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to stop doing something, as in quitting smoking.

clue.text: Sit back after cast angrily voice complaint

indicators.note: cast means thrown, and thrown letters land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word from end to start

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor sitting back angrily after casting, complaining about voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit back' comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx, an ailment that affects the voice.

clue.text: In elevator with missing female

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: lift is the British word for an elevator
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman absent from the lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sounds like a preposition, but it means burning, as a fire is still in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that is still in is still alight, so in can mean burning.

clue.text: A plea for help to tackle leading cause of cancer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to tackle someone is to grab them, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means leading or top

explanation.surface: A cancer charity appealing for help to combat the main cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading cause' looks like one phrase but 'leading' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos fibres, when inhaled, are a known carcinogen causing mesothelioma.

clue.text: Pass light over empty stage

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pale means light in colour

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of stage

explanation.surface: Shining a light across a bare theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is a verb, as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by.
